- One error in the paper itself: the comma in "says director, Penny Livingston".
- Kept after close reading:
  - "Ms. Beryl": Ms. plus a first name is standard address in preschools.
  - "It doesn’t matter that Beryl is 87, and Layla is four": the comma between two coordinated clauses is acceptable.
  - "The pair have": British collective plural, which fits the British spelling "programmes".
  - "The programmes work and even the kids’ parents benefit": short clauses, so the comma is optional.
  - "their bodies seem to benefit from staying with the children because they move more": the logic is consistent.
  - The numbers are consistent: 87 and four (an intergenerational contrast), and Maya has worked there three years.
- I could not find the source article online; the names may be invented for the exam.

**z35 (2025 Beijing D)**
- The current text matches the paper's Word file exactly, all 5 paragraphs. That docx contains only this passage, with no questions.
- I identified the source through web search snippets: Faisal Hoque, "AI Isn’t the Problem, We Are", Psychology Today (Code & Conscience blog), April 2025. Direct fetches of the page were blocked, so the source wording comes from search snippets only.
- Errors reported in the paper itself:
  - Comma splice "this way, instead, it was" (introduced by the adaptation).
  - "colored people" (offensive term, introduced by the adaptation; the source says "Black and Hispanic applicants").
  - Missing article in "in money-lending business".
  - Comma splice "biases (偏见), it is mirroring" (also in the source).
  - "making these problems seen" (low confidence; the source has "more visible").
- Kept after checking against the source:
  - "They are judging the data, rules, and beliefs" (source: "evaluating the data, policies, and assumptions"; "judge" in the sense "assess" is acceptable).
  - "the footprints of ourselves we leave in the world" (source: "traces of ourselves"; the digital-footprint metaphor is fine).
  - "if I give it up in a heartbeat to visit a website, the algorithms may make a very different judgment of what I really want" (source wording, with "judgment" for "assessment").
  - "read our principles into the record of our actions rather than allowing the two to diverge" (the source's exact wording; the metaphor is unusual but it is the author's own).
  - "how we as average people want to shape its role".
  - "A few years ago" for Amazon's 2018 decision to drop its hiring tool, and "a recent study" for the UC Berkeley lending research. Both are plausible for a 2025 paper.
  - "In both cases" correctly refers to the two examples, hiring and lending.
  - "It isn’t enough to ask how it will change us" ("it" = AI).
  - "We should not only improve AI models, but also make sure": acceptable.
